Surah 75: Al-Qiyamah (The Resurrection)

In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

﴿I do not swear by the Day of Resurrection﴾. That is: "I swear." From Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him both): the "lā" is superfluous (ṣilah), like His saying ﴿so that the People of the Scripture will not know﴾ [al-Hadid: 29], and like the verse:

In the well of Lahur he travelled by night and was not aware.

And like the saying:

"I remembered Layla, and passion seized me, and the heart's core was nearly being torn apart."

This is the view of the majority. From al-Farra': the "lā" is a rejection of the disbelievers' denial of resurrection, as if it were said: "The matter is not as you claim." Then it was said: "I swear by the Day of Resurrection." It was also said that the original form is "la-uqsimu," as in the reading of Ibn Kathir, with the lam being the lam of initiation (lam al-ibtida'), and "uqsimu" is the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning "la-anā uqsimu" ("Indeed, I swear"). What strengthens this is that in the Imam (the 'Uthmanic codex) it is written without an alif, and then it was lengthened, so an alif appeared from the lengthening. This lam is usually accompanied by the emphatic nūn (nūn al-ta'kid), though it may sometimes be omitted.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 75, verse 2:**

﴿And I swear by the self-reproaching soul.﴾ The majority (al-jumhur) of scholars hold that this is another oath (qasam). From al-Hasan (al-Basri): "He swore by the Day of Resurrection and did not swear by the self-reproaching soul, for it is an attribute of blame." According to the oath, it is an attribute of praise (p-571), meaning: the God-fearing soul that reproaches itself for falling short in piety (taqwa). It is also said that it is the soul of Adam, which never ceased to reproach itself for the act because of which it was expelled from the Garden. The answer to the oath (jawab al-qasam) is omitted, meaning: "you will certainly be resurrected," and its evidence is:

Does man think that We will not assemble his bones?

Here, "man" (al-insan) means the disbelieving denier of resurrection (al-ba'th),

"Does man think that We will not assemble his bones?" — after they have been scattered and have returned to dust (rufat), mixed with the earth.

Yes [indeed]: it (the particle "bala") affirms what follows the negation; that is, yes, We shall gather them,

able [qadirin], is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in "najma'a" (We gather); that is, We shall gather them, being able to gather them and to restore them as they were,

"to level his fingertips [bananahu]," i.e., his fingers, as they were in the world, without deficiency or disparity, despite their smallness, so how [much more] the large bones?!

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 75, verse 5:

﴿Nay, man desires to continue in wickedness before him.﴾ It is conjoined (*ʿaṭf*, coordination with a preceding element) to "Does he think" (*ayaḥsabu*), so it may likewise be interrogative (*istifhām*), like it.

﴿To continue in wickedness before him﴾: that he may persist in his wickedness in whatever time he faces in the future.
﴿He asks: when is﴾ the Day of Resurrection? — that is, "when" (matā). ﴿the Day of Resurrection﴾ — he asks as one who mocks and deems the Hour of Resurrection far-fetched.

﴿So when the sight is dazed﴾, meaning it is bewildered with terror. The reading with a fatha on the ra' (﴿بَرَقَ﴾ rather than ﴿بَرِقَ﴾) is that of "Madani" (the Medinan reader, Nafi'), and it means it stares fixedly, its gaze fixed open.

**﴿And the moon will be eclipsed﴾**, meaning its light goes away, or it sets, from His saying: ﴿So We caused the earth to swallow him﴾ [al-Qasas: 81]. Abu Haywa recited it with a *ḍamm* on the *khā'* (*khasafa* in the passive-sounding form, i.e. *khusifa*).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 75, verse 9:

﴿And the sun and the moon are joined together﴾. That is: they are joined together in rising from the west; or they are joined together in the going away of their light; or they will be brought together and cast into the sea, and it will become the Fire of God, the Greatest.

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on Surah 75, verse 10:**

﴿The human being will say﴾, meaning the disbeliever,

﴿On that Day, where is the escape?﴾ *al-mafarr* is a *maṣdar* (verbal noun, the infinitive form of the verb), meaning: the fleeing from the Fire. Or it may refer to the believer as well, fleeing from the terror. Al-Hasan recited *al-mafirr* with a kasra on the *fā’* (المَفِرّ), and it may denote either the place (*al-makān*) or the verbal noun (*al-maṣdar*).

﴿كَلا﴾: a rebuke and deterrent against seeking a place of escape,

﴿لا وزَرَ﴾: there is no refuge, no place of shelter.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 75, verse 12:

﴿To your Lord﴾, specifically,

﴿on that Day is the place of rest﴾, the resting place of the servants, or the place where they settle, either in Paradise or in the Fire, this being left to His will: whoever He wills, He admits to Paradise, and whoever He wills, He admits to the Fire.

﴿On that Day man will be informed﴾, that is, he will be told,

﴿of what he sent forward﴾, from the deeds he performed,

﴿and what he left behind﴾, that which he did not do.

(p-572) ﴿Nay, man is a witness against himself﴾. "Witness" (shāhid): the ha' (in baṣīrah) is for emphasis (mubālaghah), like in "ʿallāmah" (a great knower). Or it is feminine because he meant by it his limbs (jawāriḥ), since his limbs bear witness against him. Or the meaning is: he is a proof (ḥujjah) against himself. And al-baṣīrah means: the proof (al-ḥujjah). Allah (Exalted) said: ﴿There has certainly come to you clear evidences from your Lord﴾ [al-Anʿām: 104]. And you say to another: "You are a proof against yourself," and "baṣīrah" is in the nominative case as the subject (mubtadaʾ) of the sentence, and its predicate (khabar) is "ʿalā nafsihi" ("against himself"), which precedes it. The whole clause is the predicate of "al-insān" (man), like your saying: "Zayd, on his head is a turban" (ʿalā raʾsihi ʿimāmah). And "al-baṣīrah," according to this, may be the angel assigned to him (al-malak al-muwakkal ʿalayh).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 75, verse 15:

﴿Even if he presents his excuses﴾: he lets down his curtains. Al-Mi'dhar (the curtain, screen) means a screen. It has also been said: even if he came with every excuse, it would not be accepted from him, for he is upon himself a witness who denies his excuse. As for al-Ma'adhir (the excuses), it is not the plural of ma'dhira (excuse), since the plural of that is ma'adhir; rather it is a collective noun (ism jam') for it. Similar to it is al-Manakir (the denounced things), in relation to al-Munkar (the denounced thing).

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 75, verse 16:**

﴿Do not move your tongue with it﴾, that is, with the Qur'an,

﴿to hasten with it﴾, that is, with the Qur'an. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to anticipate Jibril in the recitation, before Jibril had finished, out of his dislike that it might slip away from him. So it was said to him: "Do not move your tongue with the recitation of the Revelation while Jibril is reciting, so that you hasten with it, so that you take it up hastily, and lest it slip away from you." Then he gave the reason for the prohibition against haste with his saying:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 75, verse 17:

﴿Indeed, upon Us is its collection﴾, in your breast,

﴿and its recitation﴾, and the establishing of its recitation on your tongue. And "al-Qur'an" (the recitation): and similar to it is: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation to you is completed﴾ [Ta-Ha: 114].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 75, verse 18:

﴿So when We have recited it﴾, i.e., when Jibril has recited it to you, and so He made Jibril's recitation His own recitation.

﴿Then follow its recitation﴾, i.e., its recitation to you.
Then indeed upon Us is its clarification (Quran 75:19), that is, if anything of its meanings becomes unclear to you.

**﴿Nay﴾**, a rebuke against denying the Resurrection, or a rebuke to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for hastiness, and a disapproval of it directed at him. He reinforced this with His words: **﴿Rather, you love the hasty life﴾**, as if it were said: "Rather, you, O children of Adam, because you were created from haste and were made of its nature, hasten toward everything, and for this reason you love the hasty life, that is, this world and its desires."

﴿And you leave the Hereafter﴾: the Last Abode and its bliss, so you do not work for it. The recitation with the *ta'* (تاء) in both verbs is that of [the readers of] Madina and Kufa (Madani and Kufi) [p-573].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 75, verse 22:

﴿Faces﴾ — these are the faces of the believers,

﴿On that Day, radiant﴾ — bright and beautiful, flourishing.

"Towards their Lord, looking" (﴿إلى رَبِّها ناظِرَةٌ﴾), without modality (بِلا كَيْفِيَّةٍ), without direction (ولا وُجْهَةٍ), and without establishing a distance (ولا ثُبُوتِ مَسافَةٍ). Interpreting "looking" (al-nazar) as "waiting" (al-intizar) for the command of their Lord, or for His reward, is not valid, because it is said: "nazartu fihi" (نَظَرْتُ فِيهِ), meaning "I reflected on it" (tafakkartu), and "nazartuhu" (نَظَرْتُهُ), meaning "I waited for him" (intazartuhu). It is not construed with "ila" (إلى, "to") except in the sense of "seeing" (al-ru'yah). Moreover, waiting is not fitting in the abode of permanence (dar al-qarar).

**Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 75, verse 24:**

﴿And faces that Day will be gloomy﴾, scowling, intensely severe in their frowning. These are the faces of the disbelievers.

﴿تَظُنُّ﴾ (taẓunnu, "she expects"): she anticipates that some act will be done to her, one which in its severity is ﴿فَاقِرَةٌ﴾ (fāqiratun, "a calamity"), a disaster that breaks the spine of the back.

"Kallā" (ﷺ no) — the particle is a rebuke against preferring the worldly life over the Hereafter. It is as if it were said: "Desist from that, and take heed of the death that lies before you, at which the transient life is cut off from you, and you are moved to the everlasting life in which you will abide forever."

﴿Idhā balaghati﴾ — i.e., the soul (al-rūḥ). Although no mention of it has preceded, this is permissible because the verse indicates it.

﴿al-tarāqī﴾ — the bones surrounding the hollow of the throat, on the right and the left. It is the plural of "tarqūwa" (collarbone).

**﴿And it is said: "Who is a healer?"﴾** Hafs pauses on "man" (مَن) with a brief pause (وُقَيْفَة). That is, those present at the dying man said to one another: "Which of you will treat him (يَرْقِيهِ) of what afflicts him?" This is from "al-ruqyah" (الرُّقْيَةُ), of the pattern of "ḍaraba" (ضَرَبَ). Or it is from the speech of the angels: "Which of you will ascend (يَرْقى) with his soul? Are they the angels of mercy or the angels of punishment?" This is from "al-ruqiyy" (الرُّقِيُّ), of the pattern of "ʿalima" (عَلِمَ).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 75, verse 28:

﴿And he thought﴾ — the dying person was certain — ﴿that it was the parting﴾ — that what had befallen him was the parting from the beloved world.

ﷻ﴿And one leg will be entwined with the other leg﴾. His two legs twist together at his death. It is reported from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib: "They are his two legs when they are wrapped in his shroud." It is also said: it is the severity of parting from the world together with the intensity of the approach of the Hereafter, and the leg is a metaphor for severity. It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: "They are two anxieties: the anxiety of family and children, and the anxiety of coming before the One, the Eternal Refuge."

(p-574) ﴿To your Lord, that Day, is the driving.﴾ It is a verbal noun (maṣdar) of "sāqahu" (he drove him), meaning: the driving of the servants to where Allah has commanded, either to Paradise or to the Fire.

﴿So he did not affirm (ṣaddaqa)﴾, meaning he did not affirm the Messenger and the Qur'an,

﴿nor did he pray (ṣallā)﴾, meaning the human being, as in His words: ﴿Does man think that We will not assemble his bones?﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 3]
﴿But he denied﴾ the Qur'an, ﴿and turned away﴾ from faith. Or: ﴿he neither affirmed [the truth]﴾ — that is, his wealth: he did not give its zakat (i.e., he did not purify it).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 75, verse 33:

﴿Then he went back to his family, swaggering.﴾ It means he strutted (yatabakhtaru). Its original form is "yatamatta" (yatamaṭṭaṭ), meaning he stretches himself out, because the one who swaggers stretches his strides. The ṭāʾ was then changed into a yāʾ (tamaṭṭaya → yatamatta → yatamattā), because of the coming together of three identical letters.

"Awlā laka" (woe to you), in the sense of "waylun laka," and it is a curse upon him that what he dislikes should befall him,

﴿Awlā﴾

Surah 75, verse 35: ﴿Then woe to you, and woe again! Woe to you, and woe again!﴾ [Note: the verse itself is quoted in the commentary as ﴿ثُمَّ أوْلى لَكَ فَأوْلى﴾; translated plainly within the markers.]

Al-Nasafi says: The phrase is repeated for emphasis, as if he said: "Woe to you, then woe! Then woe to you, then woe!" It is also said: woe to you on the day of death, woe to you in the grave, woe to you at the time of resurrection, and woe to you in the Fire.

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿Does man think that he will be left neglected?﴾ Commentary: Does the disbelieving human think that he will be left unattended, not commanded, not forbidden, not raised up, and not recompensed?

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 75, verse 37:

﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted from seminal fluid?﴾ With the letter yāʾ (yumnā), read by Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥafṣ, meaning: the seminal fluid (al-maniyy) is poured forth into the womb. With the letter tāʾ (tumnā), the pronoun refers back to nuṭfah (the drop).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 75, verse 38:

﴿Then he was a clinging clot﴾ i.e., the semen became a piece of congealed blood, after forty days,

﴿then He created [him] and proportioned [him]﴾: Allah created from it a human being in complete and proper form.

﴿So He made from him﴾, from the human being,

﴿the two mates, the male and the female﴾, i.e., from the semen, the two kinds.

(p-575) ﴿Is not He who does that able to give life to the dead?﴾ Is not the One who performs these things able to bring back (creation) again?! "When he (ﷺ) recited it, he would say: 'Glory be to You, indeed (yes)'."
